> **Project Altrabyte** is an advanced, real-time health monitoring platform designed specifically for astronauts operating in space environments. The system continuously tracks critical physiological parameters—such as cardiovascular metrics, fatigue levels, and stress indicators—using a seamless wearable sensor network powered by predictive AI analytics. It addresses the unique medical challenges of spaceflight by providing instant anomaly detection and automated early warnings. By alerting both crew members and ground control to health risks before symptoms escalate, Project Altrabyte ensures rapid intervention, mitigates long-term physiological degradation, and safeguards astronaut well-being during extended missions.
details:
Project Altrabyte (Lunar Habitat Crew Telemetry Command System) is a real-time astronaut health and habitat telemetry monitoring platform. It aggregates continuous physiological sensor streams—including heart rate variability, blood oxygen saturation, stress markers, and fatigue indicators—alongside environmental telemetry into a unified command dashboard. Using predictive analytics and threshold-based anomaly detection, the system flags early signs of physiological strain before critical thresholds are breached.

Benefits & Intended Impact Deep-space and lunar missions introduce communication delays and isolated environments where immediate Earth-based medical intervention is impossible. Project Altrabyte empowers flight surgeons and crew members with automated early warnings, actionable health insights, and rapid triage protocols—reducing medical response times and safeguarding long-term crew health.

Tools, Software & Creativity

  • Frontend & Visualization: Web-based telemetry dashboard and UI/UX prototyping tools
  • Presentation & Documentation: Gamma, Google Slides, and GitHub for version control and public hosting
  • Design Considerations: Engineered for high-contrast readability under low-light habitat conditions, zero-latency alert prioritization, and offline-first resilience during Earth-Moon communication blackouts.
